chapter: Melvin Moore, Hammond and the New York trip
title: Hobart Banks rejoins at a Longbell dance hall
summary: Back in Oklahoma Fields books western-swing barns with help from Bob Wills; the men joke about Hobart hitchhiking to the job.

bands.name: Bob Wills and His Texas Playboys

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So we played Wichita, Kansas and I was gettng on into a little area--I worked pretty close in hand--I mentioned this a little further down--with Bob Wells and the Texas Playboys, we were very good friends--the western

swing bands--so they had turned me on to a little town in western Oklahoma, Longbell, nothing but a room, but in that big barn, those country bums would come from everywhere, and I booked there and told Hobart to meet me and so he was there--it was nothing but a stop in the road-- I don't know how he got there, on the bus or something--but the boys were always kidding me, I always was a hunter, a hunter and a fisherman, that was my weakness, and most of the time carried the shotgun along with me, and they all got to kidding me when we got almost into the little town there, Hobart was out on the road like he's hitchhiking, I think Rene Hall said to me, I wish you had your shotgun.
How were you travelling, did you have a bus by then?
Yeah, I had a bus then.
Where did you get the bus?
just jumped into this Melvin Moore that I was telling you about, but I'm going to come up with when we got the bus later on.
So anyway, he said I wish I had your shotgun and some birdshot, I'd shoot him; a man who couldn't go to New York City and meets us out here ain't got no brain; what kind of brain does that man got?
